newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says banking sector fine despite failures.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says banking sector fine despite failures.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told parliament on Tuesday a rash of failures in smaller Czech banks should not be destabilising to the whole banking sector.

"Public opinion, government and the chamber are disappointed by the number of collapsed smaller banks...their impact in their absolute number is not low...," Klaus said opening the October session. "But it has not reached a level that would destabilise the Czech banking system."

Klaus said his government had made it a priority to restore faith in the banking sector, which has seen 12 banks in a sector once numbering more than 50 fall under central bank forced administration and/or failing in recent years.
"The main goal of the government is to maintain and strengthen the trust of citizens and foreigners in the Czech banking system...that's the priority task," Klaus said.
According to the central bank, more than 70 percent of Czech banking activity takes place with the largest four banks and positions at those banks are solid.

The problems of Czech banks became a political football after the failure of the small Kreditni Banka a.s. in August and the subsequent liquidity crisis at Agrobanka a.s., which had strong ties to Kreditni.

Klaus, who was forced by the opposition in parliament to accept a parliamentary probe into Kreditni's failure, said he did not agree with the view something really bad happended with the collapse of Kredtni.
He said the post-Communist market economy and banking system had started from zero and that creating a functioning banking system was a "long-term process."
